children.name: Limax
children.description: Limax — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Limax aeolianus Fo.Giusti, 1973
children.description:
External: Slug whitish, sometimes yellowish with reddish hue, covered with irregular black spots on the upper and lateral side and mantle, but not on head and neck, and a greyish lateral band-like structure; keel weak and only in posterior 15-18 mm; mantle oval, 17-19 mm long (preserved); posterior margin more pointed; sole whitish or yellowish white, subdivided in 3 longitudinal sections.

Internal: Shell oval, with nucleus laterally situated.

children.name: Limax albipes Dumont & Mortillet, 1853
children.description:
External: Slug evenly brown ot bluish black, very shiny; sole white or cream; mucus not sticky, colourless.

Internal: Penis very short, only half body length; retractor and vas deferens not opening at posterior end of penis but shortly before.

Juveniles: cloudy pattern on the mantle. .

children.name: Limax canapicianus Pollonera, 1885
children.description:
External: Slug light brown with nearly rounded black dots; mantle rounded at posterior end; pneumostome in the mid section of mantle; keel short at posterior end and weakly lighter brown than dorsum; sole evenly white.

Genitalia obviously like those of Limax cinereoniger.

children.name: Limax cephalonicus Simroth, 1886
children.description:
External: Black to black-brown to dark gray body, sometimes with a light keel/mid-line; sometimes blackish and light spots, forming reticulations or streaks across body and mantle; keel only on 1/7 of body; creamy sole; clear mucous (Wiktor 1996).

Internal: Strait or slightly bent penis, <1/2 body length; retractor and vas deferens 1/3 of the way along penis from its apex, with retractor closer to base than vas deferens; apex of penis "pocket" or "horn"-shaped; internal fold in apical half of penis (Wiktor 1996).

Similar to L. macedonicus, but penis is <1/2 body length, thicker, straight and club-shaped, with longer coecum (Wiktor 1983). .

children.name: Limax ciminensis Pollonera, 1890
children.description: External: Slug light brownish with orange hue and 4 darker colour bands; keel lighter and slightly more yellowish, extending on posterior 2/3 of dorsum; mantle light brown with some light spots on its anterior part and slightly darker spots on its posterior part; foot fringe reddish brown; sole whitish with reddish hue in medial section, lateral zones reddish brown.

children.name: Limax cinereoniger Wolf, 1803
children.description: Limax cinereoniger, also known as the ash-black slug is a large species of air-breathing land slug in the terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusc family Limacidae, the keelback slugs.

children.name: Limax conemenosi O.Boettger, 1882
children.description:
External: Narrow body; gray-cream, yellowish, or red-gray body with small black spots (1 mm) scattered evenly; slightly rounded dorsum; short, weak keel to 10 mm long; creamy sole; clear mucous.

Internal: Cylindrical penis 1/2 body length with broad coecum, with vas deferens far above connection with retractor muscle (2/3 from base); penis with strong fold inside posterior part (Wiktor 1983, 1996).

Genitalia similar to those of L. macedonicus, but penial coecum does not taper and retractor muscle thinner (Wiktor 1983).

children.name: Limax corsicus Moquin-Tandon, 1855
children.description:
External: Slug brownish ochre to dark reddish brown, with light dorsal line, margins lighter, near foot red; dorsal colour pattern can be blurred so that the animals appear unicolour; lateral zones of sole red, central zone yellowish to light red.

Eggs: Globulous, 5 mm diameter.

children.name: Limax dacampi Menegazzi, 1855
children.description: Limax dacampi (by other authors Limax dacampoi) is a species of air-breathing land slug, a terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusk in the family Limacidae, the keelback slugs.

children.name: Limax dobrogicus Grossu & Lupu, 1960
children.description:
External: Yellow-gray body (when alive and mucus-covered) with spots on body and marbling on mantle; light head and neck; bluish tentacles; short, pale keel; deep grooves in skin; wide pneumostome.

Internal: Long, cylindrical, bent penis; no penial stimulator; no rectal caecum (Grossu & Lupu 1960; Rähle 1992).

children.name: Limax erythrus Bourguignat, 1864
children.description: External: Slug reddish, slightly lighter downwards at the sides (colours will change in preserved animals); keel restricted to posterior haft section of dorsum behind mantle; mantle concentrically striated, more intensively red than dorsum, with two darker reddish brown lateral bands; margins of mantle red with orange hue; pneumostome surrounded by a blackish margin; tentacles brownish; sole yellowish with violet brownish lateral sides.

children.name: Limax gerhardti Niethammer, 1937
children.description:
External: Slug evenly black; very finely corrugated; posterior part shortly keeled; posterior end of the mantle smoothly angulated, not pointed; sole light reddish, with darker reddish margins; margin of the foot black; mucus not sticky, colourless.

Penis very long, vas deferens and retractor inserting at the distal end of the penis.

Differs from L. cinereoniger in its longer penis, a more finely corrugated surface and a shorter keel, and the black margin of the sole being narrower and less clearly delimited against the light central zone of the sole. L. punctulatus has a more uniformly coloured sole.

children.name: Limax giovannellae Falkner & Niederhöfer, 2008
children.description:
External: Slug greyish brown with weak light patterns; keel yellowish white in posterior section, in last third sharp, prominent at the posterior end; mantle evenly light brownish; sole evenly white.

Differs from Limax maximus in its thicker and more massive penis and weak caecum, from Limax veronensis in its narrower vas deferens without glands.

children.name: Limax graecus Simroth, 1889
children.description:
External: Cylindrical body and round dorsum; black at higher altitudes, brown to grey at lower altitudes, and pink to cream at coast; sometimes dark or light spots present, or banding on sides; keel same color of the rest of the dorsum; 10 mm long keel; weak skin grooves; light sole; clear mucous; (Wiktor 1983, 1996).

Internal: Penis tubular and ~2/3 body length and coiled or distinctly bent; vas deferens enters penis 1/7 from its apex, and muscular retractor is below; narrowing, strongly bent penial appendix (post-vas deferens); a strong longitudinal fold inside posterior part of penis; ovate spermatheca with short, distinct duct; oviduct 1/3 penis length and broadens toward atrium; short atrium (Wiktor 1983, 1996).

children.name: Limax hemmeni Rähle, 1983
children.description:
External: Slug ashy grey with numerous irregular yellowish spots; mantle length 35 % of body, narrowing posteriorly, not rounded but triangularly elongated; keel short; sole evenly light.

Internal: Penis short, 3/7 of body length; penis retractor muscle forked into several branches near penis; vas deferens opens apically into a hooked appendix at the posterior part of the penis; retractor branches insert at vas deferens junction and at different locations of the proximal penis section.

children.name: Limax ianninii Fo.Giusti, 1973
children.description:
External: Slug evenly black; keel very weak and restricted to the posterior 16-20 mm; mantle large (23-27 mm long), oval, pointed at posterior end; sole subdivided in 3 longitudinal sections, evenly white or yellowish white.

Internal: Penis very short (less than 26 mm, in Limax albipes up to 60-70 mm).

children.name: Limax lachensis Bérenguier, 1900
children.description:
External: Slug reddish, becoming pale yellow down to the sides, with black spots on dorsal side, simulating two lateral and one medial lines; mantle rounded in anterior part, finely black spotted, finely concentrically striated; sole evenly yellowish white with orange red margin; sole mucus colourless, body mucus reddish orange.

Internal: Shell subtriangular and shiny, very slightly convex at upper side, concave at lower side, distinctly concentrically striated, nucleus in posterior section, margin translucent; penis long and massive; spermatheca pear-shaped with short duct.

External apppearence like Limax maximus, shell like Limax cinereoniger. More research is necessary to clarify its classification, the description of the genitalia is from the 1930s and certainly insufficient.

children.name: Limax maximus Linnaeus, 1758
children.description: Limax maximus (literally, "biggest slug"), known by the common names great grey slug and leopard slug, is a species of slug in the family Limacidae, the keeled slugs.

children.name: Limax millipunctatus Pini, 1885
children.description:
External: Slug greyish or yellowish with brown-reddish hue on dorsum and mantle; entirely covered with evenly distributed numerous black dots, slightly less regular down to the sides; tubercles oval and not very prominent; keel short and not very prominent; mantle anteriorly rounded and pointed at posterior end, concentrically striated; tentacles finely spotted; pneumostome without distict margin and slighty posterior of the centre of the mantle; sole evenly white.

Differs from Limax punctulatus in its darker colour, more oval and shorter tubercles, coloured medial line in posterior section, bases of tentacles not approaching each other and lack of a distinct margin of the respiratory hole.

children.name: Limax punctulatus Sordelli, 1870
children.description:
External: Somewhat worm-shaped body; grey-brown, brown, or grey-yellow body, sometimes with black or brown spots in rows on sides, and darker mantle and dorsum; mantle may have spots; keel 1/4 body length, pale; an orange-red spot on the neck under the mantle of at least some specimens; sole cream (Wiktor 1983).

Internal: Penis >2.5x(!) body length, very coiled, contributing >1/3 of visceral mass; vas deferens 1/4 penis length; strong muscular retractor at penis apex; spermatheca long, distinct from its duct; short oviduct and atrium like L. cereoniger (Wiktor 1983).

Similar to L. cereoniger, but has longer penis, 1-color sole, weaker keel, finer grooves in skin, broader posterior body (Wiktor 1983).

children.name: Limax redii Gerhardt, 1933
children.description: External: Slug creamy or yellowish, sometimes with bluish hue, usually with scattered black dots; less dotted on mantle; head and tentacles grey; sole unicoloured.

children.name: Limax sarnensis Heim & Nitz, 2009
children.description:
External: Slug colour variable, creamy white, brownish or black, often with colour spots or bands; mantle always evenly coloured without patterns (difference to several other species).

Internal: Penis 1/3-1/2 of body length, inside with weak transverse folds and one interior pilaster; vas deferens inserts close to tip of penis, retractor attached at same point as vas deferens.

children.name: Limax spec Krauss, 1848
children.description: REGNUM ANIMALE. ANIMALIA organisatione viva, nervis sentiunt, percipiunt, seque ex arbitrio movent motu possibili. VIVENTIA singula, in multiplicatione prodiga Natura, orditur a minimis, generat in fluido, incipit in ovi liquido, cum omne vivum ex ovo. OVUM intra Tunicas, saepe includentes Albumen, continet Vitellum, cujus lateri emergenti insertum Punctum saliens, vegetans in Embryonem, caulescentem Funiculo umbilicali, radicatum placenta vitellina. MATER prolifera promit ante generationem vivum compendium novi animalis suique simillimi, tamquam plumulam intra semen vegetabile; hoc Patris polline spermatico electrisatum calore excluditur; Punctum saliens enim Ovi incubantis Avis ostendit primum Cor micans Cerebrumque cum Medulla; corculum hoc, cessans a frigore, excitatur calido halitu, premitque Bulla a � rea, sensim dilatata, liquores secundum canales fluxiles. Punctum vitalitatis itaque in viventibus est tantum a prima creatione continuata vitae ramificatio, cum ovum sit gemma matris ab exordio viva, licet non sentiens ante foecundationem; sic Generatio Aequivoca nulla. CORPUS Animantium composita est machina: Naturalis, vegetat e cranii Tubere crustato, Caule verticali, articulato, rigido, opposite ramoso, cui insident Folia carnosa, fibrosa, sparsa, apicibus etiam affixa in Musculos, prodeunte Fructificatione genitalium e dichotomia ultima caulis.

children.name: Limax squamosus Bérenguier, 1900
children.description:
External: Slug yellow with interrupted dark brown lateral bands; keel prominent and yellowish; mantle yellowish with oval black spots; foot whitish with yellowish margin.

Internal: Shell long and very narrow; penis cylindrical; vas deferens very long; spermatheca oval.

Differs from L. maximus in its yellowish bordered foot and narrow shell. .

children.name: Limax subalpinus Lessona, 1880
children.description:
External: Olive body with dark green markings forming rows of spots along the body length; large spots on mantle; keel 1/3 body length, lighter green, with black-green spots along it; dark edge of pneumostome; 3-part sole with cream center and black side sections (Wiktor 1983).

Internal: Genitalia like those of L. maximus; penis cylindrical, >1/2 body length, and convoluted but straight near the apex; retractor and vas deferens attached at penis apex (Wiktor 1983).

children.name: Limax veronensis Lessona & Pollonera, 1882
children.description:
External: Slug olive greyish (or with reddish hue?); mantle and dorsal zone of body with brown spots or longitudinal dashes; foot margin and marginal zone of sole reddish; medial zone of sole whitish.

Internal: Vas deferens not very narrow, with glands.

Cannot always be distinguished from Limax maximus.

children.name: Limax wohlberedti Simroth, 1900
children.description:
External: Thick skin with strong grooves; black body and keel; wavy keel along entire dorsum; large pneumostome surrounded by a ring; 3-part sole with dark side sections and black pigment granules therein, and light middle section (Wiktor 1996).

Internal: Penis shorter than mantle; wide penis with large retractor muscle almost at apex, next to vas deferens, sometimes with a bit of a pocket/blind end; internal wavy fold along entire length of penis; vas deferens attached to side of penis along entire length; long spermatheca with duct of similar width; spermatheca+duct = 1/2 penis length; lower half of oviduct wider than upper half; minimal atrium (Wiktor 1996).

children.name: Limax wolterstorffi Simroth, 1900
children.description:
External: Slug evenly black or dark grey, getting lighter down to the sides; narrowly corrugated keel restricted to the very posterior end.

Internal: Penis short, thick, less than 1/2 of body length.

The description was not of an excellently good quality (could have been a juvenile slug of another known species), and I have no further information concerning its identity.

children.name: Limacus
children.description: Limacus — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Limacus flavus
children.description: Limacus flavus, known commonly as the cellar slug, the yellow slug, or the tawny garden slug, is a large species of air-breathing land slug, a terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusc in the family Limacidae.

children.name: Limacus maculatus
children.description: Limacus maculatus, the green cellar slug or Irish yellow slug, is a species of slug native to the Caucasus and Black Sea coast.

children.name: Gigantomilax
children.description: Gigantomilax — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Gigantomilax brunneus
children.description:
External: Medium slugs; wrinkles flat, parallel to keel; pointed posterior edge of mantle; pneumostome postmedial on mantle (Schileyko 2003).

Internal: Large, conical flagellum on apex of penis; cylindrical or globular penis containing sphincter and longitudinal pilasters (Schileyko 2003).

children.name: Gigantomilax cecconii
children.description:
External: Medium slugs; black or dark gray body and paler tentacles; weak keel for 2/3 dorsum; peumostome medial/post-medial; pointed posterior edge of mantle; wrinkles in fan shape from mantle; creamy white sole with black spots (Schileyko 2003; Heller 2009).

Internal: Short, globular penis contains a sphincter but no stimulator; penial retractor and one retentor muscle present (Schileyko 2003).

children.name: Gigantomilax daghestanus
children.description:
External: Mantle <1/3 body length; black with dark gray sides, light gray spots in grooves; pale tentacles and neck; long, coarse “rhomboid” wrinkles; sole creamy with dark border; small pneumostome (Schütt 2010).

Internal: Small genitalia; rounded penis and short vas deferens of similar length; no rectal caecum (Schütt 2010).

Similar to G. monticola and G. koenigi but no dark markings on mantle (Sysoev & Schileyko 2009).

children.name: Gigantomilax koenigi
children.description:
External: Medium slugs; mantle ¼ body length; brown to yellow-brown body; characteristic dark brown stripes (often becoming spots), one on either side closely parallel to keel and continuing onto mantle; pale, strong keel on 2/3 dorsum before mantle; peumostome medial/post-medial and with a dark brown edge; pointed posterior edge of mantle; wrinkles in fan shape from mantle (Schileyko 2003; Schütt 2010).

Internal: Short, globular penis contains a sphincter but no stimulator; penial retractor and one retentor muscle present (Schileyko 2003).

children.name: Gigantomilax lederi
children.description:
External: Mantle 1/3 body length, rounded posteriorly; blue to bluish black body; light blue neck; black-blue spots on sides above foot fringe; pale keel extends along entire dorsum to mantle; 3-part sole with cream interior and light blue side sections; light blue mucus (Schütt 2010).

Internal: Relatively thick internal shell, 10 x 7 mm; spherical penis with internal sarcobelum; no intestinal caecum (Schütt 2010).

Juveniles: Begin as pinkish (to 10 mm long) and become gray (Schütt 2010).

children.name: Gigantomilax monticola
children.description:
External: Mantle <1/3 body length; brown body with darker brown mantle with a horseshoe band, and light keel; sides below mantle and sole cream; body darkens with age; coarse skin wrinkles; mantle with a slight angle posteriorly; little pneumostome (Schütt 2010).

Internal: Short atrium; wide penis with internal "circular roll”; short and wide vas deferens (Schütt 2010).

Subspecies: G. monticola armeniacus has genital and right tentacle retractor muscles cross, G. monticola monticola does not; there are no other differences (Schütt 2010).

Juveniles: Cream color (Schütt 2010).

children.name: Malacolimax
children.description: Malacolimax — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Malacolimax mrazeki
children.description:
External: Dark bright yellow body, with two lateral streaks on tail and mantle, and one dark medial streak on mantle; darker sides; light keel; whitish sole; black tentacles; yellow-orange mucous (Wiktor 1996).

Internal: Penis short, rounded, with wide base; penis more than 1/2 mantle length; dark, distended part at the penis apex; wide muscular retractor connects at 2/3 length of penis; folds inside penis; spermatheca long, ovate, and equal in length to its duct; spermatheca duct connects at base of penis; right ommatophore muscle goes under penis and between spermatheca (Wiktor 1996).

Morphologically very similar to M. tenellus but geographically separated. M. tenellus is lighter and smaller, with a smaller penis and a retractor on the apex rather than the side of penis (Wiktor 1996).

children.name: Malacolimax tenellus
children.description: | synonyms = Limax tenellus O.F.

children.name: Lehmannia
children.description: Lehmannia — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Lehmannia brunneri
children.description:
External: Thin body; black or dark blue body, sometimes with lighter sides, and some with black-gray markings (2 bands on each side with rows of spots beneath, and 5-7 bands on mantle) on a gray-cream background; darker specimens live at higher altitudes; head gray- or brown-cream; black tentacles; keel light; 3-part sole with gray-cream middle section and blackish side sections.

Internal: Vas deferens longer than penis and >2x length of oviduct; cylindrical penis often curved in an "S", with a darkly pigmented apical end; "penis pocket" in funnel shape becomes vas deferens and with retractor muscle at its base; long and thin penial appendix 1/2 length of penis; small spermatheca; spermatheca+duct is 1/2 penis length; long and cylindrical oviduct; differentiated, cylindrical atrium (Wiktor 1983).

children.name: Lehmannia horezia Grossu & Lupu, 1962
children.description:
External: Relatively thick bodied and with large mantle; gray-cream body with darker markings, including two bands on mantle with brown color in between, and sometimes with dark gray spots in rows along body sides; cream keel and sole (Wiktor 1983).

Internal: Short vas deferens; penis club-shaped with dark apical end and long, thick retractor muscle; long, thin penial apendix/gland >1/2 penis length and often coiled, opposite retractor; spermatheca to 2x length of penis; oviduct about penis length (Wiktor 1983).

Similar to L. rupicola but with shorter penis, longer spermatheca, shorter oviduct (Wiktor 1983). Similar to L. macroflagellata but is stouter and larger with blurred (not clear) body patterns, larger round (not flat) penis and penial gland not as thin or long (longer than penis in L. macroflagellata), larger spermatheca, and shorter duct (Wiktor 1983).

children.name: Lehmannia islandica Forcart, 1966
children.description: Lehmannia islandica was described as a species of air-breathing land slug, a shell-less pulmonate gastropod mollusk in the family Limacidae.

children.name: Lehmannia janetscheki Forcart, 1966
children.description:
External: Slug small; dark, dorsally olive grey, upside darker, with a light brown central band; mantle with a strong central colour band on light brownish brackground, two strong inner and two weak marginal bands.

Internal: Penial flagellum slender and worm-shaped, inserting at the tip and not laterally; vagina shorter than in L. marginata.

children.name: Lehmannia jaroslaviae Grossu, 1967
children.description:
External: Slug light grey with irregular white dashes on mantle and dorsum, on mantle forming bands not uniting to a horse-shoe like pattern and not being continued on dorsum; keel light, reaching mantle, but prominent only on posterior half of dorsum; sole slender, medial section narrower than lateral sections.

Internal: Shell 4.5 x 3 mm with thin margins and concentric lines; penis long but not evenly cylindrical; vas deferens opening laterally near proximal end of penis; retractor muscle inserts slightly more proximal than vas deferens in penis; posterior end of penis equipped with a well developed flagellum about 1/3 of penis length.

children.name: Lehmannia macroflagellata Grossu & Lupu, 1962
children.description: Lehmannia macroflagellata is species of air-breathing land slug, a shell-less terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusk in the family Limacidae.

children.name: Lehmannia marginata
children.description: thumb|right|A small Lehmannia marginata browsing on lichen amid moss patches Lehmannia marginata is a species of air-breathing land slug, a terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusk in the family Limacidae.

children.name: Lehmannia medioflagellata Lupu, 1968
children.description:
External: Slug reddish brown, lighter down to the sides, with a light and fine medial band and broad and uninterrupted black lateral bands; keel occupies last 1/3 of body; posterior section pointed; mantle perfectly oval with 2 broad lateral black bands (never in lyra form); sole light in subdivided in 3 longitudinal zones.

Internal: Penis short (3.5 mm); flagellum inserts laterally (not terminally) at penis, which is unusual.

children.name: Lehmannia melitensis
children.description: Ambigolimax melitensis is a species of air-breathing land slug, a pulmonate gastropod mollusc in the family Limacidae .

children.name: Lehmannia requienii Pollonera, 1896
children.description: External: Slug ochrous with blackish zones and spots; less transparent and contains less water than Lehmannia marginata; dorsum keeled in last 1/3 section; sole evenly pale.

children.name: Lehmannia rupicola Lessona & Pollonera, 1882
children.description:
External: Much like Lehmannia marginata, contains less water, basic colour brown, light dorsal colour band narrow or absent, colour differences in mantle shield.

Internal: Flagellum longer and more slender than in L. marginata, approximately as long as penis; atrium and vas deferens shorter and less slender.

children.name: Lehmannia szigethyae Wiktor, 1975
children.description:
External: Either cream body with dark patterns, or entirely black body (Wiktor 1996).

Internal: Long penis, sometimes curved into an "S"; dark structures sometimes on end of penis; no penial gland; ovate spermatheca well differentiated from its duct; narrow oviduct equal to penis length (Wiktor 1996).

Externally similar to other Lehmannia (Wiktor 1996).

children.name: Ambigolimax
children.description: Ambigolimax — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Ambigolimax valentianus
children.description: Ambigolimax valentianus (formerly known as Lehmannia valentiana) is a species of terrestrial slug, a pulmonate gastropod mollusc in the family Limacidae.

children.name: Bielzia
children.description: Bielzia — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Bielzia coerulans
children.description: Bielzia coerulans, commonly known as the Carpathian blue slug or simply the blue slug, is a species of very large land slug, a terrestrial pulmonate gastropod in the family Limacidae, the keelback slugs.

children.name: Eumilax
children.description: Eumilax — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Eumilax brandti
children.description:
External: Brown to dark brown with spots/flecks, marbling on mantle; thick skin with fine grooves; keel extends along entire dorsum to mantle; pneumostome (uniquely) anterior to midline of mantle and with raised edge; 3-part sole with lighter central region (Schütt 2010).

Internal: Short atrium; “bipartite penis” with a pointed stimulator in basal part, apical part ovate; long epiphallus; short, cylindrical spermatheca (Schütt 2010).

Juveniles: Very dark brown (Schütt 2010).

children.name: Eumilax intermittens
children.description:
External: Medium to large slugs; keel on entire dorsum; mantle more than 1/2 dorsum length; small tubercles all over upper body; pneumostome antemedial on mantle (Schileyko 2003).

Internal: No intestinal caecum; short, thin vas deferens; penis with apical short, rounded flagellum containing 2 pilasters fused at its base; very short penis; very long, curved appendix on penis; many oblique longitudinal ridges inside penis; retractor muscle attached to penis apex; long oviduct; very short vagina; spermatheca with very short duct (Schileyko 2003).

children.name: Svanetia
children.description: Svanetia — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Svanetia caucasica
children.description:
External: Small slugs; large mantle slightly less than 1/2 body length; pneumostome postmedial on mantle; keel at least 3/4 length of dorsum (Schileyko 2003).

Internal: Right ocular retractor passes under oviduct and penial retractor muscle; very short, thick vas deferens; short penis containing a large verge; short oviduct; spermatheca undifferentiated from its duct, muscular, tubular, and thick-walled (Schileyko 2003).

children.name: Turcomilax
children.description: Turcomilax — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Metalimax
children.description: Metalimax — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Metalimax elegans Simroth, 1902
children.description:
External: Medium slugs with narrow bodies; keel present; mantle 1/3 body length with a broad cephalic shield and a pointed posterior end; pneumostome antemedial on mantle (Schileyko 2003).

Internal: 3-looped intestine with long caecum on third small loop; vas deferens attached about to apex to penis; long, tubular penis; no appendix or flagellum on penis; longitudinal pilaster inside penis; short oviduct; spermatheca with minimal duct (Schileyko 2003). .

children.name: Metalimax varius
children.description:
External: Medium slugs with narrow bodies; keel present; mantle 1/3 body length with a broad cephalic shield and a pointed posterior end; pneumostome antemedial on mantle (Schileyko 2003).

Internal: 3-looped intestine with long caecum on third small loop; vas deferens attached about to apex to penis; long, tubular penis; no appendix or flagellum on penis; longitudinal pilaster inside penis; short oviduct; spermatheca with minimal duct (Schileyko 2003). .

children.name: Caspilimax
children.description: Caspilimax — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Caspilimax keyserlingi
children.description:
External: Large slugs; variable in color; mantle <1/3 body length; pointed posterior edge of mantle; pneomostome post-medial on mantle; large cephalic shield; short keel (Schileyko 2003).

Internal: Right ocular retractor passes under oviduct and penial retractor muscle; no intestinal caecum; very short, thick vas deferens joins penis through an internal pore; globular penis contains a rounded stimulator and 1-2 large folds; penial retractor muscle on base of penis; thin sheath around lower 2/3 of penis; short oviduct with short folds inside; spermatheca small with short duct; no vagina (Schileyko 2003).
